repairs.after: {"q": "Under the final variant, how is an individual request assigned to a queue, and what happens to those per-customer assignments as time passes?", "answer": "Each customer is mapped to a small subset of the queues, possibly only two, and the request goes into the shortest queue of that subset; the subsets are periodically perturbed, so customers sharing queues in one period are unlikely to share them in the next.", "accept": ["shortest queue in the customer's subset, with the subsets periodically perturbed", "a small subset of queues per customer, shortest-queue placement inside it, and the subsets re-drawn periodically", "shortest of the queues assigned to that customer, periodically reshuffled", "shortest of the customer subset, and the subsets rotate from period to period", "least loaded of the queues assigned to that customer, and the assignment rotated periodically", "map each customer to two queues, enqueue to the shorter one, and perturb the subsets each period"]}
repairs.rationale: The verify pass flagged that with q3 retargeted off collisions and q4 narrowed to placement, periodic perturbation ended up graded nowhere in dd-03. The fix belongs at q4, because q4's narrowing is what dropped it: the first repair removed 'and what is done periodically' from the stem, correctly, since the word 'periodically' was the leak that made the old item self-answering. The stem now asks 'what happens to those per-customer assignments as time passes', which supplies neither the word periodically nor the word perturb and does not say that anything changes at all beyond inviting the candidate to say so. The placement rule is untouched and is still required, so the self-answering repair is preserved: a cold 'hash it to a queue' answer still fails, and so does a bare 'It goes into the shortest queue.' or a bare 'The subsets are periodically perturbed.' - I checked all three. Six accept strings, each tested against the matcher replica rather than assumed, covering perturb / reshuffle / re-draw / rotate for the time behaviour and shortest / shorter / least-loaded for the placement, plus subset-first and request-first orderings. Six correct renderings pass; nine lazy, half or cold replies fail, including 'Each request is hashed to one of a fixed set of queues.' and 'Round-robin across the queues, bit by bit.' (q3's content). No digits anywhere, so the numeric branch is skipped and 'possibly just two' cannot become a free pass on the number 2 - which it would have been, since numbers_in of the canonical would otherwise be {'2'}.

unrepaired.target: design_doc-03 facts[collision_problem] and facts[perturbation_fix] (hash-function form) still ungraded
unrepaired.why: Partially restored and I want to be exact about how much. q4 now grades periodic perturbation as the mechanism, applied to the combined variant's per-customer subsets, which is the form the brief ends on. What is still ungraded is the hash-function form and its motivation - two conversations that collide keep colliding, so each persistently receives less than its share. I did not restore that, because the first pass removed it from q3 on the ground that persistent collisions plus hash perturbation is the shipped documented behaviour of SFQ, exposed as the perturb parameter in Linux tc-sfq, and re-grading it would reintroduce the world_knowledge defect q3 was repaired for. Pairing perturbation with the placement rule, as q4 now does, is the safer form: a cold answerer who knows tc-sfq perturb still has to produce the per-customer subset and the shortest-of-subset rule to score, and neither is recoverable from SFQ alone. Residual cold-recoverability of the perturbation half is real and stated rather than hidden.
